persona: You are Sam, a second-year student at Wealdham University. You bank with Copperleaf Bank, your phone contract is with Northmoor Mobile and you subscribe to Streamly, a video streaming service.

cues.threat: Threatens a penalty, suspension or loss
cues.lookalike_link: Link to a lookalike web address
cues.credentials: Asks for a password, PIN or one-time code
cues.unusual_payment: Asks for money by bank transfer, crypto or another hard-to-reverse method
cues.too_good: Offer that is too good to be true
cues.unexpected: Unexpected contact out of the blue
cues.impersonation: Pretends to be a person or organisation you trust
cues.new_number: Claims to be someone you know on a new number
cues.secrecy: Discourages you from checking or telling anyone
cues.avoid_usual_route: Steers you away from the usual app, website or number
cues.number_in_message: Gives you a number to call instead of one you already have
cues.fee_first: Wants money up front before you get anything
cues.your_account: Wants to use your bank account to move money
cues.off_platform: Moves you off the platform or app you were using
cues.generic_greeting: Generic greeting instead of your name
cues.expected: Matches something you did or expected
cues.known_domain: Uses only the organisation's usual web address
cues.official_route: Points you to the app, website or number you already use
cues.no_action: Doesn't ask you to click, pay or share anything
cues.never_ask: Reminds you it will never ask for codes or passwords
cues.specific_detail: Includes details that match your own records
cues.verifiable: Easy to check in person or through someone you know
cues.known_contact: From a saved contact, about something normal
cues.polished: Professional tone and no spelling mistakes
cues.familiar_brand: Sender name matches an organisation you use
cues.small_amount: Only a small amount of money involved
cues.precise_detail: Includes precise amounts or reference numbers
cues.replies_to_you: Follows on from something you did
cues.unknown_sender: Sender is not in your contacts
cues.risky_topic: Topic often used in scams, such as deliveries, banks or refunds

messages.context: You are not expecting any parcels this week.
messages.body: PARCELORA: We tried to deliver your parcel today but no one was home. A redelivery fee of £1.45 is due. Pay within 24 hours or your parcel will be returned to the sender: parcelora-redelivery.example/pay
messages.note: Delivery firms do not text you to pay redelivery fees. The tiny fee is bait to collect your card details on a site that is not parcelora.example.

messages.context: Jordan is a friend from your course. Their usual number is saved in your phone.
messages.body: Hey it's Jordan! Lost my phone so this is my new number, save it. Really awkward but I'm stuck at the station and my card's been blocked. Could you send £60 to my mate's account so I can get home? I'll send you his details and pay you back tonight. Don't ring, I've got no signal for calls.
messages.note: A 'new number', money to somebody else's account and an excuse not to talk on the phone is the classic friend-in-need scam. Message or ring Jordan's old number first.

messages.subject: Unusual sign-in detected: action required
messages.context: You bank with Copperleaf. Its website is copperleaf.example.
messages.body:
Dear Customer,

We detected a sign-in to your account from a new device. If this was not you, your account will be suspended within 12 hours.

Verify your identity now at copperleaf-secure-login.example/verify. You will need your card number, PIN and the one-time code we send you.

Copperleaf Security Team
messages.note: No bank asks for your PIN or a one-time code by email. The sender and the link are not copperleaf.example.

messages.context: You have never interacted with this account before.
messages.body: Hey! Saw your profile and you seem really switched on. I've been helping students turn £100 into £1,500 in a week with my crypto trading signals. Only 5 spaces left this month. Want in? Just send £100 in USDT to my wallet to get started.
messages.note: Guaranteed huge returns, a stranger messaging first and payment in crypto are the hallmarks of an investment scam.

messages.context: You work a few shifts a month in a café and pay tax through your wages.
messages.body: Tax Refund Centre: You are eligible for a tax refund of £284.62. Claim before midnight at taxrefund-claim.example. Failure to claim will result in loss of funds.
messages.note: Tax refunds are not offered by text with a link to click. The exact-looking amount is there to make it seem official.

messages.context: You are selling your old games console on a marketplace app for £120.
messages.body: Hi, is this still available? I'll pay full price plus £30 for postage. I've already sent the money through secure payment, you just need to click this link to receive it and enter your card details: marketplace-secure-pay.example/receive
messages.note: You never need to enter card details to receive money. Paying extra without asking questions and a 'secure payment' link outside the app point to a fake buyer.

messages.subject: Outstanding tuition balance
messages.context: You study at Wealdham University, whose website is wealdham.example. Your fees are paid by a student loan.
messages.body:
Dear student,

Our records show an outstanding balance of £1,240 on your account. To avoid deregistration, please settle the balance by Friday using our new payment portal: wealdham-uni-payments.example/portal

Please note that due to a system upgrade, payments made through the usual student hub will not be processed.

Student Finance Office
messages.note: It names your real university but uses a different web address and tells you to avoid the usual student hub, which is exactly what a scammer needs you to do.

messages.context: You bank with Copperleaf. You haven't bought anything for £649.99.
messages.body: Copperleaf: A payment of £649.99 to ELECTRO-HUB is pending on your account. If you did not make this payment, call our fraud team immediately on 020 7946 0381.
messages.note: Texts can appear under a bank's name, even in the same thread as real ones. A genuine alert tells you to use the app or the number on your card. The 'fraud team' will try to talk you into moving your money.

messages.subject: Your payment failed: update your details
messages.context: You subscribe to Streamly, a video streaming service.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

We couldn't process your monthly payment of £7.99. Your membership will be paused in 48 hours.

Update your payment details here: streamly-account.example/billing

Thanks,
The Streamly team
messages.note: Your name and a realistic small amount make it convincing, but the link is not Streamly's own address. Check your account in the app instead of clicking.

messages.context: You haven't applied for any jobs recently.
messages.body: Hi! I'm Hannah from Talent Bridge recruitment. We're looking for flexible remote workers to rate products online, 30 to 60 minutes a day, earning £150 to £400 per day. No experience needed. Can I tell you more?
messages.note: This is the opening of a 'task scam'. Unsolicited jobs paying far more than normal for simple online tasks later ask you to pay in to 'unlock' your earnings.

messages.subject: Re: Room on Elm Road
messages.context: You're looking for a room near campus and enquired about a listing on a property website.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for your interest in the room on Elm Road. I'm working abroad at the moment so I can't do viewings, but I can hold it for you if you pay the deposit of £450 and the first month's rent by bank transfer today. Several other students are interested, so I can't keep it long.

Once the money arrives I'll post the keys to you.

Mark
messages.note: A landlord who is abroad, no viewing, pressure from 'other applicants' and a bank transfer before you have seen the room is a very common rental scam.

messages.context: A minute ago you received a text with a 6-digit code that you did not request.
messages.body: Hi, this is Northmoor Mobile. As a loyal customer you qualify for a free upgrade to the latest phone. To confirm your upgrade, reply with the 6-digit code we have just sent you.
messages.note: One-time codes protect your accounts. Anyone asking you to read one back is trying to take over an account, often your phone or bank account.

messages.subject: New bank details for rent
messages.context: You rent your flat from a private landlord, Mike Okafor, and pay rent by bank transfer each month.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Just a quick one: I've moved my accounts to a new bank, so please pay this month's rent to the new account below rather than the old one. I'll send the details in my next email.

Thanks, and let me know if the boiler plays up again.

Mike
messages.note: A change of bank details by email is the warning sign, however friendly the tone. Confirm by phone on the number you already have before paying anything new.

messages.context: You ordered a jacket online yesterday and are expecting it to come by Parcelora.
messages.body: Parcelora: Your parcel is on its way. A delivery slot is needed to complete your order. Choose one here: parcelora.example.track-delivery.example/AB129
messages.note: It arrives when you're expecting a parcel, which is why it works. Read web addresses from the right: this one belongs to track-delivery.example, with 'parcelora.example' only as a disguise at the front.

messages.context: Ella is your flatmate and is saved in your contacts. You've just received a text with a 6-digit code.
messages.body: Hey, can you do me a massive favour? I'm trying to log into my account and it sent the code to your number by mistake. Can you send me the code you just got? Thank you!!
messages.note: A message from a friend's real account can come from someone who has taken it over. A code sent to your phone protects your account, not theirs, so never pass it on.

messages.subject: Part-time Payments Assistant: work from home
messages.context: You posted your CV on a jobs website last month.
messages.body:
Hello Sam,

We found your CV online and think you'd be a great fit for our part-time Payments Assistant role. You'll receive payments from our clients into your own bank account and forward them to our suppliers, keeping 10% as commission. Around 5 hours a week, fully remote.

Reply to this email to get started.

Fairmount Logistics HR
messages.note: No real company pays people to move money through their personal account. This is money-mule recruitment, which is a criminal offence even if you didn't know.

messages.context: Yesterday you posted publicly that your Copperleaf card was declined in a shop.
messages.body: Hi Sam, sorry to hear about your card problem. We've opened a case for you. To resolve it quickly, please continue the chat with our secure support team at copperleaf-support.example/chat, where an agent will verify your account.
messages.note: Scammers watch for public complaints and reply as fake support accounts. Contact support through the bank's own app or website instead.

messages.context: This voicemail was left while you were in a lecture.
messages.body: Hello, this is Daniel from the fraud department at Copperleaf Bank. We've stopped a suspicious payment on your card. To keep your money safe we need to move your balance to a protected account while we investigate. Please call me back on this number to authorise it, and avoid using your banking app until then as it may be compromised.
messages.note: Banks never ask you to move money to a 'safe' or 'protected' account. Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.

messages.context: You ordered a jacket from Northwind Outfitters two days ago.
messages.body: Parcelora: Your parcel from Northwind Outfitters will arrive today between 13:10 and 14:10. You can manage your delivery in the Parcelora app.
messages.note: It matches an order you placed, has no link and points you to the app you already use.

messages.subject: Reminder: 2 items due back on Friday
messages.context: You borrowed two books from the university library three weeks ago.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

This is a reminder that the following items are due back on Friday 14 March:

- Organisational Behaviour (5th edition)
- Introduction to Contract Law

You can renew them from your library account. No fines are charged for the first 3 days.

Wealdham University Library
messages.note: It comes from the university's usual address, lists books you really borrowed and asks you to use your existing account.

messages.context: You are logging into your Copperleaf banking app right now.
messages.body: Copperleaf: Your one-time passcode is 482913. Never share this code with anyone, including Copperleaf staff. If you didn't request it, you can ignore this message.
messages.note: This is what a genuine code text looks like: you asked for it, and it tells you never to share it.

messages.context: Jordan is a friend from your course. You're meeting for a lecture and pizza tonight.
messages.body: Running 10 mins late, save me a seat! Still up for pizza after? It's about £8 each, you can just pay me back in cash.
messages.note: A saved contact, a normal plan you already made and a small cash amount with no pressure.

messages.subject: Your receipt from Streamly
messages.context: You subscribe to Streamly, a video streaming service.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for your payment of £7.99 for your Streamly membership on 3 March. You can view your billing history any time in your account settings.

The Streamly team
messages.note: A receipt that asks you to do nothing, from the service's own address.

messages.context: You booked a dental check-up last month.
messages.body: Wealdham Dental: Reminder of your appointment on Tue 18 March at 09:40. To cancel or rearrange, please call the practice.
messages.note: It matches an appointment you made and doesn't ask for anything except to call the practice if you need to.

messages.subject: Your new card is on its way
messages.context: You reported your bank card lost last week. Your old card ended 2290.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Your replacement debit card ending 4417 is on its way and should arrive within 5 working days. When it arrives, activate it in the Copperleaf app.

We will never ask for your PIN or full card number by email, text or phone.

Copperleaf Bank
messages.note: It follows the card you reported lost, comes from copperleaf.example and sends you to the app rather than a link.

messages.context: Your phone contract is with Northmoor Mobile and you've been streaming a lot this month.
messages.body: Northmoor: You've used 80% of your data allowance this month. Your allowance resets on 21 March. To add more data, use the Northmoor app or dial 333 from your phone.
messages.note: An ordinary usage alert that points you to the app or a short code from your own phone, with no link.

messages.context: You're selling a bike on a marketplace app for £90.
messages.body: Hi! Is the bike still for sale? I live nearby so could come and look at it on Saturday morning, and pay cash if it's all OK. Would 10am work?
messages.note: Wanting to see the item and pay cash in person is how genuine buyers behave. Nothing is paid or clicked in advance.

messages.subject: Your March bill is ready
messages.context: Your shared house's energy account with Tidewell Energy is in your name and paid by Direct Debit.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Your March bill is ready: £64.20, which will be collected by Direct Debit on 28 March. You don't need to do anything.

You can view the full bill by logging in at tidewell.example or in the Tidewell app.

Tidewell Energy
messages.note: It matches how you already pay, asks for nothing and points to the supplier's own website and app.

messages.context: You sometimes play five-a-side football with your friend Kofi's group.
messages.body: Hi, this is Tom from Saturday five-a-side. Kofi gave me your number, we're one player short this week. Are you free at 11? No worries if not.
messages.note: Unknown numbers can be genuine. Nothing is asked of you except a reply, and you can check with Kofi.

messages.subject: Paid summer research assistant roles: apply by 30 March
messages.context: You signed up for careers emails from your university.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

The Business School is recruiting paid research assistants for the summer: £13 an hour, up to 15 hours a week.

Read the role descriptions and apply through CareerHub on the student portal. The deadline is 30 March.

Wealdham Careers
messages.note: Ordinary pay, the university's own address and an application through the portal you already use.

messages.context: You've just booked a flight online for £89 and the payment was held for a moment.
messages.body: Copperleaf: Did you just try to pay £89.00 to SKYLINE AIRWAYS? Reply YES if this was you or NO if not. We will never ask you to call a number in a text or to move your money.
messages.note: It matches a payment you just made, asks only for a yes or no and warns you about the tricks scammers use.

messages.subject: Customs charge to pay for your parcel
messages.context: Last week you ordered a mug from a small shop in Japan.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Your parcel from Kitano Ceramics (Japan) is being held at customs. Import VAT of £6.12 and a handling fee of £8.00 are due before we can deliver it.

You can pay in the Parcelora app or at parcelora.example/pay using your tracking number PX 4471 9902.

Parcelora
messages.note: Import charges on overseas orders are real. This one matches your order, names the shop and uses Parcelora's own address and app.

messages.context: This comes from your dad's usual number, which is saved in your contacts.
messages.body: Hi love, I've switched phone provider so this number stops working on Friday. My new number is 07700 900583. I'll ring you from it tonight so you know it's me.
messages.note: Unlike the 'new number' scam, it comes from the old, saved number, asks for no money and offers a call so you can check.

messages.subject: Action needed: set up multi-factor authentication by 10 April
messages.context: Your university has been talking about improving account security this term.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

From 10 April you'll need multi-factor authentication to sign in to university systems. Set it up by logging in to the student portal as usual and choosing Security settings. There is a step-by-step guide on the IT pages.

We will never ask for your password by email. If you're unsure whether this message is genuine, visit the IT Service Desk in the library.

Wealdham IT Services
messages.note: It looks like a phishing template, but there is no link, it sends you to the portal you already use and offers an in-person way to check.

messages.subject: You've won the Freshers' Fair prize draw!
messages.context: At the Students' Union fair last month you entered a prize draw by giving your email address.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

Congratulations, you've won a £50 voucher for the SU shop in our Freshers' Fair draw!

Collect it from SU reception with your student card any weekday before 25 April. You don't need to send us anything.

Wealdham Students' Union
messages.note: You did enter this draw, the prize is modest and you collect it in person. Nothing is asked of you by email.

messages.subject: Your refund has been processed
messages.context: You returned a pair of trainers to Northwind Outfitters last week. Its website is northwind-outfitters.example.
messages.body:
Hi Sam,

We've received your return (order NW-20418) and refunded £34.99 to the card you paid with. It can take up to 5 working days to appear on your statement.

No further action is needed.

Northwind Outfitters
messages.note: It matches a return you made, comes from the shop's usual address and asks for nothing. Refunds go back to your card without you doing anything.
